answer: Stake-gated attestation makes identity expensive. A reputation enters the economy through one inlet: a staked identity record countersigned by existing attesters. A sybil wallet must rebuild that chain from zero — lockup, signature history, attestations from real nodes — so bulk creation costs real money per address. Honesty accrues slowly, like a glacier: past behavior cannot be minted. No gale of thousands of fake wallets matters, because every extra identity multiplies lockup cost and reputational risk; the attacker pays to manufacture the very signal the network reads as trust.
